newsitem.title: USA: Ethical hires Lehman, ends UK listing plan.
newsitem.headline: Ethical hires Lehman, ends UK listing plan.

text.p: Ethical Holdings Plc said Monday it had withdrawn plans for a listing on the London Stock Exchange and had appointed the investment banking firm of Lehman Brothers to assist it in exploring a variety of potential alternatives to enhance shareholder value.
Ethical also said that the proposed acquisition of Clonmel Healthcare Ltd, which was conditional on the London listing, will not proceed.

Geoffrey Guy, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement, "In light of adverse and competitive market conditions in London, we now consider that a London listing is not the most appropriate means to realize our primary objective of securing maximum shareholder value."

He said that "despite the withdrawal from the London listing, we anticipate the company's product development programs to remain on their current course and indeed these continue to expand at rapid pace."
The company said it would continue to rely on its existing network of contract manufacturers, including Clonmel, to satisfy projected manufacturing requirements.
The British-based drug development company had announced in May that it had agreed to buy Irish pharmaceutical group Clonmel Healthcare for an estimated 14 million sterling.
